findings.title: Unknown wanted end can produce a false “caught up” result
findings.description: When a product has a configured tier and start date but neither a configured end nor a dataset edge, `_wanted_end` returns `None`. In that case `_scope` includes only sessions touched by held units, but this call still tells `caught_up` that a wanted range exists. If the held sessions are complete, the command can report “caught up: yes” without evaluating the configured wanted range. Treat an unknown end as an unknown caught-up state, or otherwise define and evaluate the intended scope.

findings.title: Status and coverage lack a load test for database-backed reads
findings.description: These new commands read the tick database and production calendar, and status may process all sessions and units in scope. The added tests cover functional behavior, but the load-test suite has no status or coverage test exercising a realistic configuration with latency, throughput, or resource bounds. The project’s Python rules require a load test for network paths; add one for these read paths.
